fixes.explanation: Waiting is what you do with a timer and a hot oven. The confession says something else: “We have sinned and rebelled…” They aren't waiting in this line. They're owning up to God in heaven.

Rejoicing is a different mood from this one, friend. The people are confessing, “We have sinned and rebelled…” Everything around that line is heavy, with anger, tears and enemies. It's a confession, not a party.

I see why that might sound right, but the verse says the opposite. The people pray, “We have sinned and rebelled; You have not forgiven.” Those are their own words in the prayer. It's a hard thing to say to God, and I think that's why it hits so hard.

That's right, baker. The prayer says, “We have sinned and rebelled; You have not forgiven.” They don't tell God He has already forgiven them. They say the hard part straight, with nothing sugarcoated.
It's the other way around, friend. The writer says, “All our enemies open their mouths against us.” Mouths open, not shut. Not one of these foes is described as silent.
That's right. The writer says, “All our enemies open their mouths against us.” These foes aren't quiet. Their mouths are open against his people.

The foes leaving isn't the stopping point he names. The writer says his eyes overflow “…until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.” The end he gives is the LORD looking down, not the enemy's exit.

True, and that's the verse word for word: “My eyes bring grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.” His grief is tied to the daughters of his city. I think this man carries his whole city with him.
Yes. The writer says, “I called on Your name, O LORD, out of the depths of the Pit.” He calls from the depths of the Pit, right where he is. That's the part I'd bake into a plaque.
He does the opposite, friend. The writer says, “I called on Your name, O LORD, out of the depths of the Pit.” From the depths of the Pit, he's calling. Quiet doesn't win this verse.
True. The writer says, “You defend my cause, O Lord; You redeem my life.” Notice how the verse sits right after the LORD drew near. His words here are about what the Lord does.
